name: The Novelists of the Nineteenth Century
description: The century when the novel became the main form of storytelling: from Austen's drawing rooms to Tolstoy's battlefields and Dickens's London.

checkpoints.name: The first novelists
checkpoints.note: Austen perfects the comedy of manners, Shelley writes Frankenstein, and Pushkin shows that Russian can be a language of great literature.

checkpoints.name: The age of realism
checkpoints.note: Balzac and Stendhal map French society, Dickens and the Brontës fill British homes with serials, and Melville, Poe and Gogol work at the edges of the real.

checkpoints.name: The great novels
checkpoints.note: Eliot, Flaubert, Dostoevsky and Tolstoy write long books about conscience, while Twain and Verne attract readers with adventure and humour.

checkpoints.name: The turn of the century
checkpoints.note: Chekhov, Hardy and Wilde end the century in quiet gloom or sharp wit, leaving the stage for the modern writers who follow.
